title: Critique: if experiences explain no behavior, others' experiences are explanatorily redundant

statements.text: Belief in other minds rests on inferring mental causes from behavioral effects, which epiphenomenalism denies. Others' behavior has a physical explanation, so positing experiences in them is redundant, and each person could as well be the only one subject to this quirk of nature.

sources.quote: epiphenomenalism implies the (exceedingly implausible) conclusion that we do not know that others have mental events
It is explanatorily redundant to postulate such states for others.
